frameworks.name: Passion-Angle White Space Framework
frameworks.definition: Identify all existing passions, then find the larger adjacent market where that passion-angle has no passionate competitor — rather than limiting yourself to the market you are already passionate about.

claims.text: Greg Short (founder of Bloom Nutrition) argues that founders should not limit themselves to the market they are directly passionate about, but should instead identify which adjacent or larger market has no passionate competitor — what he calls the white space. His original passion was nutrition and supplements for men, but the white space was the female market, where incumbents were data-driven rather than passion-driven.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: Founder has genuine passion in a category
Adjacent or larger market exists where incumbents follow data rather than passion
claims.mechanism: Passion-led founders invest discretionary energy incumbents cannot match because incumbents optimize for the market signal rather than the customer experience; passion creates product and brand qualities that data-driven firms cannot prioritize when the data says those qualities are outside the core market.
bounded_by: Does not apply when incumbents in the adjacent market are themselves passion-driven
Requires genuine, transferable passion — not manufactured interest in a profitable segment

claims.text: Greg Short asserts that Bloom Nutrition won its market category because it competed against publicly traded companies and boardroom-driven incumbents who were following the data and following the market, whereas Bloom was following passion and attacking the market. In short, passion-based attack outperformed data-based optimization in a consumer supplement category.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: Consumer brand category where emotional resonance with the customer matters
Incumbent competitors are publicly traded or boardroom-governed firms optimizing against market data
claims.mechanism: Boardroom-governed firms respond to market data signals, which by definition lag the market and exclude uncommercial passion-driven decisions; a founder acting on passion makes investments that the data would not yet sanction, creating a window of asymmetric differentiation.
bounded_by: May not hold in purely commodity or price-driven markets where passion does not shift purchasing behavior
Advantage narrows once the passion-led firm grows large enough to require data governance

claims.text: Greg Short distinguishes two competitor operating modes: data-following (incumbents track what the market signals and optimize accordingly) versus passion-following (founder attacks the market from a place of genuine enthusiasm for the outcome). He positions these as mutually exclusive sources of competitive action and attributes Bloom Nutrition's category win specifically to the passion mode.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
claims.speaker_term: following the fucking data / following passion
conditions: Founder is the primary strategic decision-maker
claims.mechanism: Data-following optimization converges on the same moves as every other data-aware competitor; passion-following enables decisions that data would not recommend, keeping the brand distinct by definition.

examples.text: Greg Short's original passion was nutrition products, fitness supplements, and health and wellness aimed at men. When he looked at the market through the lens of where his passion-angle had no passionate competitor, he identified the female supplement market as the white space. He redirected Bloom Nutrition into that space and credits this pivot — entering a market his data-driven competitors did not prioritize emotionally — as the primary reason Bloom won against publicly traded supplement companies and boardroom-governed rivals.

practices.text: When selecting a market, do not confine yourself to the market you already inhabit; map all your passions and find the larger adjacent market where your passion-angle creates white space — where established, data-driven competitors have no emotional investment.
